title: Lower-left quadrant characterization
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a function from sign vectors of length $n$ to signs, and let $a$ be a real coefficient vector. Suppose $f(x)$ is the sign of $\sum_{i<n}a_i x_i$ for every sign vector $x$, and this sum is never zero. For every pair $(x,y)$ of sign vectors, the vector $\sum_{i<n}(a_i x_i,a_i y_i)$ lies in the lower-left quadrant if and only if $f(x)=f(y)=-1$.
